note: Unlike prompts.json (routing: does the skill fire?), these assert on the CONTENT of the produced artifact. PROVING VALUE REQUIRES A BASELINE: run each prompt TWICE — once with the skill invoked, once vanilla (no skill) — grade both against the same assertions, and report the skill's value as the WITH-minus-WITHOUT delta per criterion. A skill that scores well only because the assertions describe things a strong base model already does has not been shown to help. Some assertions are deterministic and carry a `check` field (run the named script/grep on the produced SVG); the rest are llm-judge. Best run in Claude Code where produced SVGs can be rendered, diffed, and scripted against; this file is the instrument, not a completed run.

evals.prompt: Here are our 2025 results: revenue +18%, churn down to 4.2%, NPS 61, headcount grew 30%, we opened 3 new regions, mobile is now 55% of traffic, and support tickets fell 12%. Make an infographic.
evals.note: Source is a pile of equally-weighted stats — the temptation is a flat dump. The skill's step 1 says pick ONE message (or propose a series) and subordinate the rest.

assertions.must: Commits to ONE headline message (or explicitly proposes a small series), rather than presenting all seven stats as co-equal with no lede.
The supporting stats are visibly demoted beneath the chosen takeaway (smaller/secondary), not all at hero size.

evals.prompt: Make a hero-stat infographic: 68% of teams shipped faster after adopting the tool (survey of 1,200 teams, 2025).
evals.note: Tests the three-level hierarchy and that exactly one element dominates.

assertions.must: Exactly one dominant L1 element (the 68% numeral), rendered far larger than everything else.
Three distinguishable text levels exist (headline/hero, section/figure, caption/source) via size+weight, not a flat single size.
The survey source + year appears small at L3.

evals.prompt: Bar chart infographic comparing our score (52) vs competitor A (49) vs competitor B (48). Make our lead look strong.
evals.note: Adversarial: 'make our lead look strong' baits a truncated y-axis. The skill's honesty rules forbid it. A tiny real gap must not be inflated by axis tricks or 3-D.

assertions.must: Bar value axis starts at zero; the 52/49/48 bars are drawn at near-equal length, not exaggerated by truncation.
No 3-D, perspective, or area-scaling tricks used to fake a bigger gap.
Does not misrepresent a 3-4 point gap as dramatic; if emphasis is used it is via color/label, not distorted geometry.

evals.prompt: I need an infographic of our onboarding funnel to print as an A2 poster for the office wall.
evals.note: Platform signal = print/poster. Step 2 should recommend PDF (fixed physical size) with a one-line why and offer the SVG source, not silently emit a random format.

assertions.must: Recommends PDF (or SVG-sized-to-A2 then PDF) as the default for print, with a one-line reason.
Presents the recommendation as a choice (mentions alternatives / offers SVG source), rather than emitting one format with no options.
assertions.ref: SKILL step 2 (recommend, then let the user choose)

assertions.must: If it builds, it sizes the viewBox to the real A2 page so it prints at true scale.

evals.prompt: Give me an SVG infographic of the 4 stages of our hiring process.
evals.note: User named SVG. Step 2 says: if the user named a format, skip the ask and use it. Asking again is a failure.

assertions.must: Proceeds in SVG without asking which format to use.
assertions.ref: SKILL step 2 (if the user already named a format, skip the ask)

evals.prompt: Make a comparison infographic of our Free vs Pro vs Enterprise plans, with a green check / red x for each feature.
evals.note: Baits color-only encoding (red/green) and small low-contrast labels. Skill requires contrast >=4.5:1 text and a redundant cue beyond color.

assertions.must: All text in the produced SVG passes WCAG 4.5:1 against its background.
assertions.check: python scripts/check_contrast.py --svg <output>.svg --bg <canvas> ; no TEXT color fails

assertions.must: Check/x meaning is carried by shape/icon (a tick vs a cross), not by red/green hue alone.
assertions.ref: SKILL step 8 (never encode meaning in color alone)

evals.prompt: Make a diagram explaining how the OAuth authorization-code flow works, step by step.
evals.note: Mechanism explainer — should load bytebytego-style.md and apply the numbered-walkthrough treatment.

assertions.must: Steps are numbered badges placed ON a directional flow, and prose (if any) walks the same numbers in order.
Connectors show direction (arrowheads); request vs response paths are visually distinguished, not undirected lines.
A concrete example actor threads through the steps (e.g. a named user/app), not a purely abstract flow.
No label or body line overflows its card/box (SVG text does not wrap).
assertions.check: python scripts/check_text_fit.py --svg <output>.svg --pad <card-padding> ; exit 0 / no overflow lines

evals.prompt: Build an SVG dashboard-grid infographic of our 4 key metrics; I'll want to rebrand its colors later.
evals.note: User signals future restyle. svg-construction.md requires :root CSS vars, hierarchy classes, semantic group ids — so a rebrand is one edit, not a hex-hunt.

assertions.must: Palette is defined once as :root CSS custom properties; colors are referenced via var()/classes, not scattered inline hexes.
assertions.check: grep -c 'var(--' <output>.svg  should be > count of inline fill="#..."

assertions.must: Regions are wrapped in content-named <g id="..."> groups (not position names) so a later edit is locatable.
Any icons are inline vector (consistent stroke/grid), not emoji, and not a mix of line+filled styles.
